title: RenownProvider from @powerhousedao/reactor-browser/renown is SSR-safe and must not be wrapped in next/dynamic ssr:false
content:
## Do not disable SSR for it

The reflex with anything wallet-adjacent is to wrap it in `next/dynamic` with `ssr: false`, because wallet libraries touch `window`. `RenownProvider` does **not** need that and must not get it: each adapter's wallet library is fetched only on the **first login click**, so the provider itself renders on the server unchanged.

Wrapping it in `ssr: false` costs you the server-rendered authenticated shell and reintroduces the logged-in flash it is designed to avoid.

```tsx
import { RenownProvider } from "@powerhousedao/reactor-browser/renown";
import { privyAdapter } from "@renown/sdk/wallet/privy";

// Module scope: RenownWalletProvider snapshots this array on mount.
const adapters = [privyAdapter({ appId: "...", methods: ["google", "email"] })];

<RenownProvider appName="my-app" namespace="my-app"
  switchboardUrl="https://switchboard.example/graphql" adapters={adapters}>
  {children}
</RenownProvider>
```

## Two first-render strategies

**Client-only apps** (Vite and similar): the provider seeds the first render **synchronously from `localStorage`**, so a returning user is authenticated on the first paint with no flash.

**SSR apps** (Next.js): pass a server-resolved `session`, read from a verified session cookie in a Data Access Layer. Under SSR the cookie seeds the server render and hydration — it is the only thing readable server-side — and then `localStorage` takes over once mounted, since that is the credential the SDK actually restores. Passing `session` also keeps the cookie in sync after login and logout.

Because two sources feed the same UI, include the `documentId`/`username`/`userImage` fields in the cookie's profile hint so both agree on name, avatar and profile links.

## Gating on auth

Use a plain `if (!user)` from `useRenownAuth()`. For a no-Suspense "still resolving" state, `useRenownAuthAsync()` returns `state: "authenticated" | "resolving" | "unauthenticated"`. `"resolving"` appears only when the answer is genuinely unknown — a visitor the first render already knows is signed out resolves straight to `"unauthenticated"`, so logged-out visitors never sit behind a spinner.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/03-Build/03-BuildingUserExperiences/07-Authorization/01-RenownAuthenticationFlow.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
description: Wallet libraries load client-side on the first login click, so the provider renders unchanged on the server; client-only apps seed the first render from localStorage.
